name: SIR epidemic
description:
Kermack and McKendrick's epidemic model: susceptible people S are infected at rate β·S·I/N, and the infected I recover at rate γ, into R, where they stay. Infection and Recovery are ordinary transfers whose rates read the compartments, so the diagram is the model and S + I + R stays at N = 1000. With β = 0.3 and γ = 0.1 a day, the basic reproduction number R0 = β/γ is 3. One case starts it; the epidemic peaks around day 38 with 301 people infected at once, exactly when S has fallen to N/R0 and R_eff passes through 1; and by day 160 about 94 % of the population has had it.

Try: lower beta to 0.15 (R0 = 1.5) and watch the peak flatten and come later. Below R0 = 1 the infection dies out.
